question.text: In 1999, this large territory became a separate territory from the Northwest Territories.
question.clue: Although not a province, this Canadian territory is the newest, having been created in 1999 as a territory for the Inuit peoples.

swap.text: A Canadian leader of this surname led the Upper Canada Rebellion but had his forces defeated at the Battle of Montgomery. The grandson of this man was the Canadian PM during the Second World War
swap.answerHtml: Mackenzie (also accept Alexander Mackenzie or William Lyon Mackenzie King)
swap.clue: An explorer with this surname was the first European north of Mexico to travel overland to the Pacific and was granted an extra share in the North West Company after having traversed 1,075 miles of a river that would later be named for him.

question.leadin: Give the following about famously terse replies in history.
question.text: Pierre Trudeau held this political position during Quebec's October Crisis, when he restricted civil liberties in the name of security. When a reporter asked how restrictive he would get, Trudeau replied, "Just watch me."
question.answerHtml: Prime Minister of Canada (prompt on partial answers like “prime minister” or "leader of Canada")
question.clue: An ad that drew attention to one candidate's Bell's palsy failed to prevent the leader of the Progressive Conservative party from being elected to this position.

swap.text: This British major general died after being shot three times during the Battle of the Plains of Abraham. This "Hero of Quebec" was memorialized in a painting by Benjamin West.
swap.clue: He served as quartermaster during an attack on Rochefort in which he was unable to convince John Mordaunt to execute a frontal assault.

question.leadin: Several members of the Liberation Cell were given safe passage to Cuba despite their involvement in this event.
question.text: Identify this 1970 event in which the FLQ kidnapped James Cross and Pierre Laporte, leading to the implementation of the War Measures Act.
question.clue: Robert Bourassa appeared on television five minutes prior to a deadline in this event stating that his government would not negotiate, resulting in the retaliatory execution of Pierre LaPorte, who had been kidnapped along with James Cross.

swap.text: This French general captured numerous English forts around Lake Champlain, including Fort Oswego and Fort William Henry. He died in the same battle as his rival, General Wolfe.

question.text: The SNC-Lavalin affair is causing problems for this party in the 2019 election, and could help other parties, such as the Conservatives or the NDP win. This is the party of Prime Minister Justin Trudeau.
question.answerHtml: Liberal Party of Canada [accept Parti libéral du Canada]
question.clue: A request to dissolve parliament by a leader of this party was refused by Governor-General Julian Byng in 1926.

swap.leadin: Identify these things about the English colonies in America.
swap.text: This act was one of the intolerable acts. It allowed freedom of religion in Canada and granted the namesake colony land west of the Appalachian.
swap.clue: This 1774 act allowed the free practice of Catholicism in its namesake colony, and also defined the boundary for that colony.

question.leadin: It occurred on the namesake plateau on September 13, 1759.
question.text: Name this battle which saw the death of British commander James Wolfe and secured control of Quebec for the British.
question.answerHtml: Battle of the Plains of Abraham [or Battle of the Heights of Abraham]
question.answer: Battle of the Plains of Abraham
question.clue: It resulted in the death of both commanders: for the French, the Marquis de Montcalm, and for the British, James Wolfe.

swap.text: Some Haudenosaunee believe "Iroquois" to be derived from the language of this tribe. This tribe fought the Haudenosaunee in the Beaver Wars and name a lake whose Manitoulin Island was sacred to the Anishinaabe.
swap.clue: Many of these people banded together with the related "Tobacco People," or Petun, after a 1648 attack that killed the Jesuit Jean de Brebeuf.

question.leadin: This group's advocacy prompted the Canadian government to request a clarification for Section 24 of the British North America Act, 1867.
question.text: Name this group of women's rights activists who were the petitioners in the Persons case. This group, which included Irene Parlby and Louise McKinney, is also named after the western province where they initially convened.

swap.leadin: This scandal saw officials wanting to build a railway bribe members of a country's first government. FTPE.
swap.text: What scandal saw Conservative members of parliament resign after taking bribes to ensure the creation of a transcontinental railroad in North America?
swap.clue: Shortly after this event, secret ballots were introduced and Sandford Fleming was appointed by the Department of Public Works to ensure that certain parts of an enterprise were built publicly.

question.leadin: This man replaced Louis Saint Laurent as Prime Minister, ending 22 years of Liberal rule.
question.text: Name this Canadian prime minister who passed the Canadian Bill of Rights in 1960. He cancelled the Avro Arrow project after agreeing to accept Bomarc nuclear missiles from the United States.
question.clue: He also cancelled the Avro Arrow program, halting production of fighter jets in his country, when he signed NORAD with the US. Raised in Saskatchewan, he passed his country's Bill of Rights, and presided over the opening of the St. Lawrence Seaway.

swap.leadin: Nardwuar the Human Serviette asked this man a question about pepper spraying protesters, to which this man evasively responded, "for me, I put pepper on my plate."
swap.text: Name this world leader whose other awkward interactions with civilians include a time when he put Bill Clennett in a chokehold.
swap.clue: Attack ads against this Prime Minister appeared to make light of his Bell's Palsy.

question.leadin: A group led by Queen Yagowania, the Erie people, were completely wiped out during this series of wars.
question.text: Name this series of wars of expansion that a Native American confederacy fought to gain access to supplies of its namesake trade good. This series of wars was ended by the Treaty of La Grande Paix.
question.clue: The Iroquois defeated the Huron in this series of wars sparked by competition for the fur of a certain animal. These wars ended with the signing of the Great Peace of Montreal.

swap.leadin: This agency guarded the border between Alaska and the Yukon Territory during the Klondike gold rush.
swap.text: Name this Canadian agency originally created to instill governmental authority in the lawless western regions of the country. This agency's members wear red serge uniforms and today, despite its name, often drive cars.
swap.answerHtml: Mounties [or Royal Canadian Mounted Police; or RCMP; or Gendarmerie Royale du Canada; or GRC; accept Royal North-West Mounted Police or RNWMP]
swap.clue: This Canadian national police force originated from the need to stop American whiskey traders from operating within the Northwest Territories.

question.text: During Mulroney's tenure as Prime Minister, he signed the Meech Lake Accords with this man, the Premier of Quebec.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about a man who unfortunately is not Charles Tupper, but did replace Charles Tupper as the prime minister of Canada.
swap.text: This French-Canadian leader protested Laurier's decision to contribute troops to South Africa, and opposed conscription under Robert Borden which he referred to as "blood tax." The founder of Montreal's Le Devoir paper, he popularized the notion of a "pact of two founding peoples."

question.text: Conrad Black gave up Canadian citizenship to take one of these things after a legal battle with Jean Chretien ("crate-YEN"). The Nickle Resolution bars Canadians from these things, which name a never-ratified amendment to the US Constitution and are banned in the first sentence of the Emoluments Clause.
question.answerHtml: titles of nobility [accept foreign peerages, knighthoods, baronetcies, orders, honors, decorations, or medals; accept Titles of Nobility Amendment or Canadian titles debate]

swap.leadin: This man worked with the Baring Brothers to secure financial backing for a railroad that connected Halifax to Windsor.
swap.text: Name this publisher of the Novascotian and Morning Chronicle who accused local politicians of stealing over 30,000 pounds from the public treasury, then was acquitted in a landmark 1835 trial affirming the freedom of the press in Canada.
